We search fractional discrete step functions of length

    h = (h_0, ..., h_{n-1}), dx = 2/n,

with constraints

    0 <= h_i <= 1,   sum_i h_i = n/2,

and objective

    C(h) = dx * max_m C_m(h),   C_m(h) = np.correlate(h, 1-h, mode="full")[m].

This is a nonconvex box-constrained minimax problem: h is fractional and many correlations are tight near the current local optimum. Existing methods proposed in this task mostly estimate a smooth scalar score (soft-max of lag scores) and then repeatedly move pieces of mass between individual coordinates, mainly using random or greedy two-coordinate transfers. They are valuable, but their acceptance of only local pair moves causes poor escape once many lags are simultaneously tight. Low-dimensional two-point moves cannot fully make room for a structure whose active constraints are correlated over neighboring lags, whereas very small coordinate moves isolate these interactions. The plan has a very direct purpose: seek a coordinated active-lag minimizer before proposing any points.
